quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
rationale: The planner flagged this rule as likely absent, but Section 10(a) (p0047-p0051) contains a broad Vendor indemnity in AP's favour that satisfies the preferred position. Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against third-party Claims arising out of (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iii) Creative placed via the Auction Platform, (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. IP infringement is covered twice over: the "Services" and "Auction Platform" prongs are unqualified and contain no IP carve-out, and prong (iv) captures Kubient's express warranty at p0033 that the Service and deliverables "do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party." Prong (v) also reaches Kubient's negligence and wilful misconduct, and p0035 plus prong (iv) cover data-security failures by Kubient. Section 11 (p0053-p0055) supplies standard procedure: prompt written notice with express confirmation that delay does not relieve the indemnifying party, indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to no admission of liability against the indemnified party without consent, and cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost. Commercially, the indemnity is stronger than our fallback: p0027 expressly carves indemnification out of the mutual consequential-damages waiver, and a search for any aggregate liability cap returned nothing, so Kubient's indemnity is uncapped rather than limited to 3x annual fees. The only divergence from the preferred position is that Customer's indemnity at p0052 is reciprocal in structure (unauthorised use of the Services/Platform, breach of rep or warranty, Content and Properties, and acts or omissions of Customer) rather than narrowed to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. That mirrors Kubient's own prongs, and Customer already accepts sole responsibility for Content and Properties at p0025 and warrants their non-infringement at p0043-p0044, so the allocation is symmetric. Given the Vendor-side indemnity is uncapped and broader than our model language, reopening this balanced clause to trim Customer's side would be disproportionate and risks unravelling a bargain that favours us. No redline proposed.

quote: (c) The relationship of the Parties is that of independent contractors, and nothing herein is intended, nor should be construed, to create a partnership, agency, joint venture or employment relationship. No act or statement of either Party will operate to bind the other and neither Party will hold itself out or have any authority as an agent of the other for any purposes whatsoever.
rationale: Exhaustive review: we read all 75 paragraphs of the Agreement in full (not keyword search alone) and confirm there is no non-solicitation, no-hire, anti-poaching or inducement covenant anywhere. The General Provisions block (p0063-p0073) and the Confidentiality section (p0056-p0061) - the two places such a covenant customarily sits - contain none; the survival list at p0070 likewise identifies no restrictive covenant. Literal searches for "solicit", "employ", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "engage", "personnel" and "non-compete", plus a regex for "(shall|will) not (solicit|hire|employ|engage|induce)", return nothing responsive. The only employment-related provisions are the independent-contractor/no-agency clause quoted above (p0066), the mutual indemnities covering third parties "hired by, employed, retained or under" a party's control (p0051-p0052), and the need-to-know disclosure limit at p0061; none restricts The Associated Press from soliciting or hiring Kubient personnel. Our preferred position - no non-solicit binding the Customer - is therefore already met, so no redline is proposed and the rendered text is identical to the original. The deterministic sub-checks for a general-solicitation carve-out and a duration of 12 months or less cannot pass and are non-probative: both presuppose an existing covenant, and satisfying them would require inserting a non-solicit that does not exist, which would create a new restriction against our own client. We will not add one. If Kubient later proposes a non-solicit, our fallback is a mutual clause limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of that involvement, with carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches, and no no-hire.

verification.notes: general-solicitation carve-out present: failed Claimed status is compliant and the cited paragraphs (confidentiality, independent-contractor, severability/survival) contain no non-solicitation, no-hire, anti-poaching or inducement covenant, so the preferred position ('No non-solicit on Customer') is met on the face of the text. Consistent with a compliant finding, the rendered text is identical to the original and no counterparty comment is proposed — the correct outcome, since adding a non-solicit would create a new restriction on our own client. The failed deterministic sub-checks (duration ≤ 12 months; general-solicitation carve-out) are non-probative here: both presuppose an existing covenant and cannot be satisfied by absence, so they do not undermine the verdict. Rationale is accurate and internally consistent, documents the fallback for future negotiation, and correctly notes that the survival list at p0070 identifies no restrictive covenant.

ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

verification.notes: The cited termination-effects provision (p0019–p0022) indeed contains no transition assistance, no return/export of Customer Content or data, and no deletion certification, so the 'missing' status is correctly characterized for a hosted auction-platform service that stores Customer data. verification.notes: The claimed deviation is supported by the cited text: Section 9(b) contains substantive warranties (industry standards, error-free, Laws compliance) running for the Term, and Section 13's disclaimer expressly carves out warranties 'set forth in this Agreement', so the only real gap is the absence of any express remedy and of a professional/workmanlike performance standard — exactly what the redline addresses. The insert is minimal and correctly located: a new sub-clause (xii) appended after existing (xi) in p0041, continuing the existing numbering of the Section 9(b) list, with no unnecessary rewriting of surrounding text or of the disclaimer (which needs no change given the express carve-out). The added language reaches the playbook position: workmanlike/industry-standard performance warranty plus repair, replacement, re-performance or refund of fees, and it is expressly non-exclusive of Customer's other rights, which is more favorable to us than the model language's default. The failed deterministic check on a 90-day/12-month period is a phrasing artifact, not a substantive defect — the existing warranties run 'throughout the Term' with no expiry, which exceeds the preferred 12-month/90-day durations, so no period needs to be inserted. proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement imposes use restrictions on us in paragraph 6 but says nothing about how Kubient may verify compliance, so we have added our standard limits: once per twelve months, 30 days' notice, an independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site review, no access to our systems, and Kubient's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%. We can accept 15 days' notice and a 10% cost-shift threshold if that is easier for you.

ops.text: Verification. If Kubient wishes to verify Customer's compliance with the use restrictions in this paragraph 6, Kubient may do so no more than once in any twelve (12) month period, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours, and only through an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than paragraph 12. Any such verification shall be conducted off-site by review of records and written responses provided by Customer wherever practicable, shall not include any direct, remote or on-site access to Customer's systems, networks, databases or facilities, and shall be at Kubient's sole cost and expense unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts properly due.

proposal.summary: Add a verification subsection to paragraph 6 capping any Kubient audit of Customer compliance at once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, off-site, by an independent auditor, at Kubient's cost, with no access to Customer systems.

quote: Customer agrees that it will not transfer or (unless expressly and specifically approved by Kubient in advance and in writing) allow third-party access to the Service.
rationale: Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "examine" and "books" return no hits, and a full read of §§ 1-14 confirms the Agreement contains no express audit right against AP: p0001 is service-delivery cooperation, p0002 our inbound licence, p0025 a use-restriction covenant, and p0035/p0045 database-security reps. The rule is therefore unsatisfied by absence rather than by adverse drafting, and I am reporting it as missing rather than compliant so the playbook's parameters actually appear on the page. The reason this is worth an edit: paragraph 6(a) imposes substantive, audit-prone use restrictions on us (no transfer, no third-party access, no reverse engineering, no service-bureau use, privacy-policy requirements) and makes us "responsible and solely liable" for Content and Properties, but is silent on how Kubient may verify compliance. Silence is not protection - it leaves the frequency, notice, cost and system-access questions open to be resolved by demand or by implication, which is the walk-away risk this rule guards against. The redline inserts a new paragraph 6(b) fixing the preferred position with a single minimal insertion and no change to existing text: one verification per twelve months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, independent third-party auditor under confidentiality no less protective than paragraph 12, off-site review of records wherever practicable, express exclusion of any direct, remote or on-site access to our systems, networks, databases or facilities, and Kubient's sole cost unless an underpayment by us exceeds 5%. The comment offers the fallback (15 days' notice, 10% threshold). Out of scope for this rule but noted for a vendor-side records rule: Impressions are measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share depends on Kubient's collections (§ 5), yet we have no reciprocal verification right - a gap in our favour to pursue separately.

verification.notes: Directionally wrong for our side: the rationale itself confirms the Agreement contains no audit, inspection or verification right against Customer, yet the redline affirmatively grants Kubient a new verification right. AUDIT is a constraining rule on a vendor right; where that right is absent, the customer is already better off than the preferred position and no edit is warranted. The premise that 'silence is not protection' is not supportable — absent an express grant, Kubient has no contractual basis to demand audits or system access, so the walk-away risk (unlimited/unannounced audits, remote access) is not live. Creating the right and then bounding it hands the counterparty leverage it did not have. Correct handling is to record this as compliant/not-applicable internal evidence (no redline, no counterparty comment), not as a 'missing' deviation requiring an insertion. The comment invites negotiation on notice period and cost-shift threshold for an audit right the counterparty never asked for, which risks anchoring a worse outcome than the current silence. Deterministic checks passing (frequency limited, operation applies) only confirm the inserted text matches the parameter template; they do not cure the fact that the insertion is adverse to the party we represent.
